title: Design exercise: SAA-3.4-S01
scenario: Copperleaf Credit Union's core ledger runs on a mainframe in its own data centre, and it is building a member web portal in one AWS Region that must read from and post to that ledger. Only the web tier of the portal may be reached from the internet; the application and account-data tiers must have no path from the internet, although the application servers need to fetch operating-system updates from public mirrors. Losing one Availability Zone must not remove any tier. Regulators forbid member data from crossing the public internet in normal operation, yet a 350 GB nightly reconciliation batch between the data centre and AWS must finish within 6 hours even while the dedicated link is down, when an encrypted internet path is acceptable.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Finance funds one dedicated 1 Gbps circuit only, so resilience for the nightly batch cannot come from a second dedicated circuit
The first release uses one VPC, and the portal goes live in 12 weeks, so the circuit's installation lead time is already accepted
Every tier must have resources in at least two Availability Zones

rubric.label: No tier is lost when one Availability Zone fails, only the web tier can be reached from the internet, and the other tiers can still fetch operating-system updates

Member data uses a private, non-internet path in normal operation, and the 350 GB batch completes within 6 hours both normally and with the dedicated link down, with the rate each path must sustain stated (about 0.13 Gbps)

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
